A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HE-GNN research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison, including matching renumbered and relocated material.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original ZINC-12k prediction results and strongly regular graph classification experiments in Table 1 and Figure 3.

after.justification: Section 6 reports original prediction and graph classification experiments, expanded comparisons, and new time and memory measurements in Figure 4.

M1.justification: The recursive individualization, embedding concatenation, message passing, and radius restriction procedures in Sections 3–4 are unchanged. The added example and execution-cost discussion explain the existing architecture rather than introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Strongly regular graph coverage expands from (26,10,3,4) to also include (29,14,6,7), (36,14,4,6), and (40,12,2,4). This broadens structural coverage within the existing isomorphism-classification task; ZINC-12k and the task types remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds PNA, Tinhofer-augmented GIN, and random-ID GIN baselines. Its former F-GIN comparator is retained under the name F-GNN. Figure 3 now includes ID-GNN, F-GNN, and T-GNN, whereas v1 displayed F-HE-GNN(1) alongside the proposed models. These additions substantially broaden the evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: ZINC evaluations add radii 1 and 2 at depths 1 and 2, beyond the existing radius-3 configurations. The SRG plot retains only radius 1 rather than the previous radius-1–5 sweep. New resource profiling measures a single forward pass without gradients, using batch size 20 and feature dimension 256; the stated training budget remains unchanged.

E4.justification: The analyses substantially change focus: Table 1 expands ZINC depth/radius sensitivity, and new Figure 4 examines how both parameters affect time and memory. Conversely, v1’s SRG radius-sensitivity analysis is removed from Figure 3 and replaced by comparisons across graph families.

E5.justification: V1 Figure 3 explicitly reports averages and standard deviations over ten runs, with error bars. V2 removes those bars and the SRG run-count/uncertainty description. ZINC’s ten-run reporting remains. This establishes reduced reporting, not that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: Shared ZINC scores are unchanged, but Table 1 adds results including PNA 0.207, GNN+T 0.199, random ID 0.226, and four HES-GNN configurations. SRG results are replaced and expanded: HE-GNN(2)’s displayed test precision on (26,10,3,4) changes from approximately 0.6 to 1.0, without establishing identical run conditions. Figure 4 adds resource measurements.

T1.justification: V2 adds Theorem 5.5, establishing strict separation of HE-GNN-1 from WL-IR-1, with a supporting graph pair and proof in Appendix D. It also adds computational-cost derivations and revises IR proofs, including Lemmas D.2–D.3. The new strictness conjecture in Section 5.3 includes d=0, which conflicts with the retained HE-GNN-0/GNN/WL equivalence.

C1.justification: The abstract now explicitly qualifies the headline logical characterization by bounded graph degree. The introduction extends the empirical superiority claim to probabilistic IR methods and emphasizes full isomorphism invariance. The central architecture, hierarchy, and homomorphism-count contributions remain.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new separation result as evidence that hierarchical combination adds expressiveness beyond parallel individualization, and states consequences for graph cospectrality. It also attributes T-GNN’s generalization failure to non-invariance and identifies strictness at greater depths as unresolved. The existing efficiency and trainability limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: V2 documents the new profiling setup: batch size 20, feature dimension 256, and forward-pass measurements excluding gradients. It also explains depth-first execution and embedding storage. The existing 256-dimensional models, maximum 1000 epochs, 20GB GPU, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: A new Related work discussion substantially expands positioning against probabilistic structural features, positional encodings, random IR traversals, and Tinhofer methods. Added citations include Franks et al., Pellizzoni et al., and Rattan and Seppelt. HE-GNN’s deterministic invariance and relationship to spectral distinguishability receive new emphasis.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites portions of the abstract and introduction, adds a Related work subsection, expands explanatory passages, and moves acknowledgements before the references. Local wording and proof exposition are revised, while the overall section sequence and most appendix text remain.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redesigned from a radius-sweep chart into a grouped comparison across four graph families. Table 1 expands substantially, Figure 4 adds time/memory plots, and Appendix Figure 5 introduces the separation example. Figure 1 moves, while the existing appendix diagrams and Table 2 are retained with relocation or renumbering.

improvement.justification: The new separation result clarifies the relationship to IR, while broader comparisons and resource profiling strengthen the evidence for expressiveness and practical feasibility. These gains are tempered by lost SRG uncertainty reporting, Section 6’s incorrect statement of 100% T-GNN test precision despite Figure 3 showing that value for training, and the new conjecture’s inconsistent d=0 case. The net improvement is useful but limited.
